- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) over recent days, model tends to underpredict true prices; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to compensate for sentiment-driven volatility.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day average), model often overcorrects downward; reduce forecast dip by 1–2% to avoid premature mean reversion.
- If model consistently underpredicts in 30-day horizon (especially when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive), add 2–4% to forecast to account for lagged momentum.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive (e.g., +0.5+), model often fails to catch the rally; increase forecast by 1–3% in next 5–7 days to reflect sentiment momentum.
- If true outcome is significantly below model (e.g., >10% gap), check if sentiment was positive recently — if so, model may be overconfident; reduce forecast by 1–3% to align with sentiment drift.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows early mean reversion (e.g., 2–3 days after peak), model often overestimates decline; adjust downward by 1–2% to reflect reality.
